mod-description: Gear-driven workshop machines and limited automation.
handbook-text-fluid-pipe-copper:
Each copper pipe stores up to 10 litres of liquid. Steam is stored as standard litres and can be compressed beyond 10 litres. A connected network accepts one content type at a time. Placement, wrench changes, and attachment removal are refused when they would join filled networks with different contents.

Ports
A newly placed pipe opens only toward the block it was placed against. Crouch while placing to open the opposite face instead. When the opened face meets another pipe, that pipe opens its matching face too. Use a wrench on a pipe face to open or close that port.

An open port aimed into air is a visible outlet. Liquid and steam are rendered inside its hollow arm. Side and bottom outlets spill liquid; a top outlet keeps the pipe's 10 litres and releases only overflow. Any air outlet vents steam above atmospheric pressure.

Pressure is measured in kPa. Liquid falls and pools in low pipes. A full vertical column adds about 9.8 kPa for every block of height, so an elevated tank can supply pipes below it and push liquid back upward as far as its water level permits. Empty and nearly empty pipes provide a small suction that helps drain the last liquid from connected pipes. Steam pressure rises with its stored amount and temperature.

Attachments
rightmouse click a free, unconnected face with plain glass to install an inspection window. The liquid shown behind it rises with the pipe's stored amount. Steam fills the visible interior and becomes more opaque as more is compressed into the pipe. The content occupies the center and every opened arm, so the view remains consistent from different angles. While content moves, its texture scrolls toward the lower-pressure side and speeds up as the pressure-driven flow rises. This display exaggerates the movement so pressure differences remain easy to read.

Install a brass sprinkler only on the bottom face. Install a copper pipe nozzle on any free face. A pipe port or attachment occupies that face. Sneak and rightmouse click an attachment with an empty hand to remove it.
handbook-text-creative-fluid-pump: This creative-only source supplies a selected Vintage Story liquid or Gearwright steam at 0-1000 kPa. A setting of 0 stops it. Steam enters at 100°C. The source fills connected pipes until their pressure reaches its setting. Sources configured for a different content cannot inject into a filled network.
handbook-text-passive-fluid-pump: The Gravity Drain is deprecated by the stored-content pipe system. It is no longer craftable, no longer appears in the creative inventory, and does not supply a pipe network. Use a copper pipe nozzle against an unsealed liquid container instead.
handbook-text-sprinkler-brass:
Install the sprinkler on the bottom face of a copper pipe. It works only with liquids and consumes the liquid stored in that pipe. It waters the first farmland found one to four blocks below each covered position. Reach is circular: radius 1 below 25 kPa, radius 2 from 25 kPa, radius 3 from 50 kPa, and radius 4 from 75 kPa.

Performance reaches 100% at 100 kPa. Fresh-water use rises with it, from 4 L/day at 50 kPa to 8 L/day at 100 kPa. The brightened, translucent spray matches the liquid stored in the pipe. Other liquids still spray, but affected crops become dead crops on their next growth attempt. Steam does not pass through a sprinkler.
handbook-text-fluid-pipe-intake-copper:
Install the copper pipe nozzle on any free pipe face. Against an unsealed Vintage Story liquid source or sink, it automatically transfers liquid in whichever direction reduces the pressure difference. It refuses liquid containers while the network contains steam.

A side- or downward-facing nozzle aimed at air drains liquid into an eternally empty output, deleting it from the world. An upward-facing nozzle aimed at air is an overflow: it keeps the pipe's 10 litres and releases only incoming liquid that will not fit. Steam vents through any air-facing nozzle only while its pressure is above the surrounding atmosphere.

Flow particles are brightened, translucent, and match the pipe contents. Outgoing flow produces a visible jet whose launch speed rises to four times its base speed at high flow. Incoming particles appear throughout a short cone in front of the opening, travel without gravity to its center, and disappear there. Pipe placement, pipe removal, attachment installation, and attachment detachment use different sounds. Sneak and rightmouse click an attachment with an empty hand to remove it.
handbook-text-pottery-profile-tool: This creative-only item is currently used to check Gearwright's item models and textures. It has no gameplay action yet.
pipe-content-conflict: That change would join pipe networks containing different contents.
hydraulic-status-running: Pipe network is settling pressure and contents.
hydraulic-status-waiting-for-chunks: Waiting for connected chunks to load.
hydraulic-status-mixed-content: Connected pipes contain different contents; transfer is stopped.
hydraulic-status-mixed-sources: Different sources are trying to fill this empty network.
hydraulic-status-content-mismatch: A connected source or container has the wrong content.
hydraulic-status-gas-container-blocked: Steam cannot enter a Vintage Story liquid container.
hydraulic-status-invalid-content: The selected pipe content is unavailable.
hydraulic-status-no-source: No usable liquid container is connected.
hydraulic-status-reserve-reached: The old horizontal reserve has been reached.
hydraulic-status-deprecated: This Gravity Drain is deprecated; use a Copper Pipe Nozzle.
